prose_updates.tldr: Fixed-size cluster counts reveal only degree-\(m\) Bernstein moments of latent four-cell exposure--outcome laws, so the cluster-equally-weighted ATE is generally an interval rather than a point. Each hierarchical SCM carries \(\mu\in\mathcal P(K_{\epsilon})\), draws \(Q_i\sim\mu\), and calibrates the observed four-cell law to \(Q_i\). For every relative-interior count law, the sharp interval has attained generalized-moment primal and Bernstein-polynomial dual programs, with compatible endpoint SCMs using at most \({m+3\choose3}\) latent laws. Its worst-case width is \(2d_m(\epsilon)\), and the shifted-Chebyshev construction gives \(0<d_m(\epsilon)\leq\operatorname{sech}(m\operatorname{arcosh}(1/(1-2\epsilon)))\leq(1-2\epsilon)^m\), with the last inequality strict for \(m\geq2\). A generic contact-hull theorem characterizes equality with valid degree-\(m\) count-measurable envelopes and gives strict improvement regions. Exact multinomial likelihood inversion yields a semialgebraic ATE confidence set recoverable by terminating CAD, and the entire relative boundary admits a finite truth-invariant semialgebraic stratification with constant identification-dimension and minimum endpoint-support labels.

project_justification.fill: The paper derives the sharp primal--dual interval, proves an iff Bernstein-span identification frontier and strict width throughout the relative interior, constructs finite-latent endpoint SCMs, and identifies the exact worst-case width as \(2d_m(\epsilon)\) with the full shifted-Chebyshev bound \(0<d_m(\epsilon)\leq\operatorname{sech}(m\operatorname{arcosh}(1/(1-2\epsilon)))\leq(1-2\epsilon)^m\), the final inequality being strict for \(m\geq2\). It gives an exact contact-hull criterion and strict improvement regions for every valid degree-\(m\) envelope, with the scalar-reference count-law-only Lee--Weidner transplant as a corollary. It also turns exact multinomial inversion into a one-dimensional semialgebraic confidence set with terminating CAD recovery and proves a finite truth-invariant semialgebraic stratification of the entire relative boundary, including constant identification-dimension and minimum endpoint-support labels on each cell.

prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: No concrete CAD run, concretely executed boundary atlas, or practical-runtime evidence is supplied. The CAD results establish exact termination and algebraic endpoint and witness recovery in principle for fixed rational inputs. The boundary theorem proves a finite truth-invariant semialgebraic stratification of the entire relative boundary, but it does not provide a uniform symbolic endpoint-witness map over positive-dimensional cells; a separately supplied algebraic boundary law instead requires specialization and a fresh terminating QE/CAD run. The full displayed shifted-Chebyshev guarantee is retained, but exact asymptotics of \(d_m(\epsilon)\) beyond the proved worst-case-width identity and upper bound are a separate future project. Heterogeneous plate sizes are also outside the present scope.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The central identification theorems concern relative-interior count laws and fixed finite \(m\). The Dirac-fiber proposition records point-identified boundary images for \(m\geq2\), so strict width is not asserted on the boundary. The boundary-fiber-atlas theorem nevertheless proves, for the entire relative boundary, a finite truth-invariant semialgebraic stratification on whose cells identification dimension and minimum lower- and upper-endpoint support sizes are constant; it also supplies a terminating construction with defining formulas, labels, and sample-point witnesses. What remains outside scope is a concretely executed atlas, practical CAD runtime guarantees, and a uniform symbolic endpoint-witness map over positive-dimensional cells. Whole-set coverage is only the immediate corollary of exact count-law coverage and the defining confidence-set union, not an independent solve target. The exact \(m=1\), \(\epsilon=1/4\), uniform-count proposition is a sanity check. Exact asymptotics of \(d_m(\epsilon)\) beyond the proved worst-case identity and shifted-Chebyshev upper bound, as well as growing or heterogeneous plate-size extensions, belong to separate future projects.
